---
title: 'Test strategy'
description: 'Which tests the platform keeps, which CI lane runs each one, and when a unit test is the wrong tool. End-to-end user journeys are the primary regression coverage.'
updatedAt: '2026-11-27'
audience: developers
---

End-to-end user journeys are the primary regression coverage. A journey asserts
something a user can observe, such as signing in, opening the Tasks board, or
joining a Meet as a guest, and it keeps passing through refactors that do not
change behaviour. Unit tests that pin implementation details fail on changes
that are not regressions, add CI time, and push authors to update fixtures
instead of reading the failure.

## Keep unit tests for

- Pure logic: parsers, validators, state machines, and status engines.
- Money and time math: currency rounding, time zones, and DST boundaries.
- Security and auth boundaries: token verifiers, permission checks,
  app-coordination and session gates, route auth wrappers, and the protected
  workflow guards.
- Database and RLS contracts: policy and migration checks in the database
  lane.

## Do not add or keep

- Golden or pixel snapshots as the regression signal for copy, spacing,
  layout, or colour. Use a journey assertion on the visible state instead.
- Source-text scans: reading CSS, workflow YAML, route directories, or message
  files and matching strings in them.
- Inventory counts: asserting how many routes, pages, apps, or workflows exist.
- Pinned configuration literals such as shard counts, matrix values, and
  timeouts. Assert the invariant instead, for example that `--total-shards`
  equals the matrix length and every shard index is covered once.
- Mock-heavy UI tests that rebuild the component tree to check markup.

When a test in the list above guards a real boundary, keep the boundary and
move the assertion onto behaviour (a request that must be rejected, a value
that must be computed) rather than onto text.

## CI lanes

| Lane | Workflow | Role |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Unit and script tests | `turbo-unit-tests.yaml` (`Test`) | Required. Pure logic, security boundaries, contracts. |
| Mobile | `mobile.yaml` | Required. Flutter analysis, then Flutter tests in shards. |
| Web E2E | `e2e-framework-report-only.yaml` | Report-only. Deterministic replay with `--strict-cache` and zero model calls. |
| Type, lint, security, database | `type-check.yaml`, `oxc-check.yaml`, `security-checks.yaml`, database contracts | Required and unchanged. |

Playwright suites stay authoritative until the pilot decision in
[E2E pilot and Playwright retirement](/build/development-tools/e2e-pilot-decision)
is applied per suite.

## Writing a journey

Journeys live under `apps/web/e2e-agent/` and use `e2e`. Record the trace once,
commit `.e2e/cache`, and let CI replay it. The setup, fixture identity rules,
and agent MCP workflow are in the
[Agentic E2E Framework](/build/development-tools/e2e-framework) guide.

## Deleting a test

Every deleted test needs one of the following in its commit message:

- the name of the journey that now covers the same behaviour, or
- a written reason that no behaviour is lost, with the boundary it guarded.

Do not delete a security or database contract to make a lane faster. Move it to
the lane that owns it.

## Rollout

Existing golden, inventory, and source-scan suites are retired in slices. Each
slice names the journey or invariant that replaces each deleted test, and its
commit carries the review and CI evidence for the lane change.

## Measuring CI time

Measure wall time per workflow and per job on `main` before and after a
change:

```bash
gh run list --repo tutur3u/platform --branch main --workflow mobile.yaml --limit 20 \
  --json databaseId,conclusion,createdAt,updatedAt
gh api repos/tutur3u/platform/actions/runs/<run-id>/jobs --jq \
  '.jobs[] | {name, conclusion, started_at, completed_at}'
```

Compare medians rather than single runs. A lane that is cancelled or queued
is not a timing sample.
